newsitem.title: UK: European insurers face tougher competition - report.
newsitem.headline: European insurers face tougher competition - report.

text.p: Europe's insurance market is set for a period of rapid change as liberalisation and greater competition make their mark, Swiss Re said in a report.

"Insurance companies will attempt to seize market shares from other suppliers via greater price and client segmentation," the reinsurer said in a report entitled 'Deregulation and liberalisation of market access: the European insurance industry on the threshold of a new era in competition.'
Government regulation now has only a limited role to play -- mainly in solvency control -- leaving market forces as the key determinant of prices, the report said.
The introduction in July 1994 of legislation allowing insurers with a licence in one European Union state to operate in all EU countries will also open up the market to greater competitive pressure.
"Freedom to fix prices, alternative sales methods and tougher competition from new suppliers are already putting pressure on premium rates and margins," Swiss Re said.

Companies with a weak capital base will come under particular pressure, but established insurers could also lose market share to specialised and direct operators taking advantage of new opportunities.
"The example of the British and French markets shows that the market dominance of the major insurers may even decline, leading to greater fragmentation of the market," the report said.
